findings.problem: PacketWorkflow struct allows any combination of status, is_validated, and is_sent fields. A packet can be marked sent without being validated, or have status 'draft' while is_sent is true. All lifecycle states are independently mutable.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can construct PacketWorkflow{status: "draft", is_validated: false, is_sent: true, ...} which represents a logically impossible state — a packet that is both unsent and sent simultaneously, or sent before validated. This state can propagate silently through the system.
findings.fix: Replace status: String, is_validated: bool, and is_sent: bool with a single PacketState enum that encodes valid transitions (e.g., Draft, Validated, Sent). Remove the individual boolean fields. Make the struct fields private and provide smart constructors.

findings.problem: status: String is used for lifecycle state tracking. Strings allow arbitrary values like "sent", "SENT", " Sent ", "pending", or "" that have no meaning in the packet lifecycle domain.
findings.failure_mode: A string field can hold any value the caller chooses. There is no compile-time guarantee that status is a valid lifecycle state. Pattern matching on the status requires string comparison, which is error-prone and cannot exhaustively cover valid states.
findings.fix: Replace status: String with a #[derive(Copy, Clone, Debug, PartialEq)] enum PacketState { Draft, Validated, Sent }. Update all transitions to use enum variants instead of string literals.

findings.problem: is_validated: bool and is_sent: bool are independent lifecycle booleans. They can be true simultaneously, both false after reset, or any arbitrary combination, violating the lifecycle invariant that validation must precede sending.
findings.failure_mode: Both flags can be true at once (sent without explicit validation), both false after a reset operation, or is_sent can be true while is_validated is false. The booleans encode a temporal ordering that Rust types do not enforce, making it possible to reach invalid lifecycle combinations.
findings.fix: Replace both booleans with a single typestate enum that encodes the lifecycle as distinct states (Draft, Validated, Sent). Each state transition is a function that returns the new state, making illegal transitions compile-time errors.

findings.problem: sent_at_epoch_ms: Option<u64> can be None while is_sent is true, or Some(timestamp) while is_sent is false. The optional timestamp is decoupled from the sent state it semantically belongs to.
findings.failure_mode: A packet can be is_sent: true with sent_at_epoch_ms: None, meaning the packet was sent but has no timestamp — a data integrity violation. Conversely, sent_at_epoch_ms: Some(0) with is_sent: false is nonsensical. The Option is an invalid-state vector.
findings.fix: Move the timestamp into the typestate enum itself. Use an enum variant like Sent { timestamp: u64 } instead of a separate Option<u64> field. This makes the invariant — a sent packet always has a timestamp — a type invariant.

findings.problem: id: String is a raw primitive with no domain constraints. Any string value including empty, whitespace-only, or malformed IDs can be assigned. There is no validation or newtype wrapper to enforce ID invariants.
findings.failure_mode: A caller can set id to "", "  ", or any malformed string. Downstream code cannot assume id is a valid packet identifier without repeating validation checks at every use site.
findings.fix: Replace id: String with a newtype struct PacketId(String) that has a private field and a fallible constructor: impl PacketId { fn new(id: &str) -> Result<Self, ParseError> { ... } }. Make the id field private in PacketWorkflow.

findings.problem: Raw primitives (String, bool, Option<u64>) are exposed directly in the public struct. There is no parse boundary — no fallible smart constructors, no domain type validation at the boundary. Callers can construct invalid PacketWorkflow instances directly from raw data.
findings.failure_mode: External callers (deserialization, HTTP handlers, CLI) can pass raw strings and booleans directly into PacketWorkflow fields, bypassing all domain invariants. The struct is a data dump that accepts illegal states at the parse boundary, violating the parse-don't-validate principle.
findings.fix: Introduce PacketId::new() for fallible ID parsing, PacketState enum replacing status+booleans, and a PacketWorkflow::builder() or PacketWorkflow::new() that constructs the domain type from validated inputs. All fields must be private with a single entry point.

findings.problem: mark_sent accepts any PacketWorkflow regardless of its current state and blindly overwrites status and is_sent. There is no guard against calling mark_sent on a packet that hasn't been validated, or on a packet already in the sent state.
findings.failure_mode: mark_sent can be called on a Draft packet, skipping validation entirely. It can also be called multiple times on the same packet, each call resetting the state. There is no state machine enforcement — any state can transition to sent, and sent->sent is idempotent in an uncontrolled way.
findings.fix: Replace mark_sent with a method on the typestate enum: impl PacketState { fn validate(self) -> Result<PacketState, TransitionError> { ... } fn mark_sent(self) -> Result<PacketState, TransitionError> { ... } }. Each transition is fallible and enforces preconditions.

findings.problem: All fields of PacketWorkflow are pub, allowing external code to mutate status, is_validated, and is_sent directly without going through any transition logic.
findings.failure_mode: Any crate consumer can write `item.is_sent = true` directly, completely bypassing mark_sent and all lifecycle invariants. Public fields make the struct immutable by accident — the type system cannot enforce that transitions go through proper channels.
findings.fix: Make all fields private. Provide methods or builder pattern for state transitions. Use `#[doc(hidden)]` or private constructors to prevent direct struct construction from external crates.

no command evidence: cargo fmt, cargo check, cargo clippy were not run
no behavior tests exist for state transitions, invalid state prevention, or lifecycle invariants

residual_risk: The entire domain model is violated — PacketWorkflow admits every illegal state combination through raw primitive fields. The mark_sent function enforces no lifecycle invariants. There are no tests, no benchmarks, no parse boundary, and no typed error taxonomy. Delivery is completely blocked until the typestate machine, parse boundary, and error types are implemented and verified.
